title: Enhancing singlet oxygen yield in π-extended BODIPY dyes through strategic  meso -thienyl substitution: a computational and experimental study
content: Two new poly-thienyl BDP dyes have been synthesized by solventless reactions. The dyes include extended π-systems from naphtho-pyrrole units shifting their electronic absorption beyond 600 nm with high molar absorptivities. The poly-thienyl BDP dyes, 2TBDP and 3TBDP, along with a previously studied meso-thienyl BDP (1TBDP) show that addition of thienyl moieties significantly affects their fluorescent quantum efficiency. Singlet oxygen studies using 1,3-diphenylisobenzofuran (DPBF) as a singlet oxygen quencher show that addition of thienyl groups results in significant increases in singlet oxygen quantum yields. Computational studies further suggest that conformational effects modulate singlet–triplet spin–orbit coupling (SOC), influencing the propensity for intersystem crossing. An analysis using a relative ISC rate metric, based on the ratio of squared SOC to squared singlet–triplet energy gaps, reveals increased propensity for ISC in 2TBDP compared with 1TBDP, with 3TBDP exhibiting a substantially greater propensity than both dyes. These findings are consistent with the enhanced triplet-state-mediated photosensitization observed upon thienyl substitution.
